declarations.name: Causal.Causality.iUnion_Iminus_eq_of_dual_pastInextensible
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u} [TopologicalSpace M] {C : Causality M} {W : Opens M}, (∀ (I : Set ℝ) (γ : ℝ → M), C.dual.PastInextensible W I γ → (∀ a ∈ I, ∀ b ∈ I, C.dual.ChronalCurveOn W γ a b) → ⋃ t ∈ I, C.dual.Iplus W {γ t} = ↑W) → ∀ (I : Set ℝ) (γ : ℝ → M), C.FutureInextensible W I γ → (∀ a ∈ I, ∀ b ∈ I, C.ChronalCurveOn W γ a b) → ⋃ t ∈ I, C.Iminus W {γ t} = ↑W
declarations.what: The converse of dual_iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_futureInextensible (:330), placed directly after it, in the same variable context and with the same binder shapes: its hypothesis is that lemma's conclusion and its conclusion that lemma's hypothesis. No separation axiom and no other hypothesis. Probe.lean checks that the two give an iff: `⟨dual_iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_futureInextensible, iUnion_Iminus_eq_of_dual_pastInextensible⟩`.
declarations.proof: The twin's argument with the order reversed. For γ future-inextensible for C over I, `dual_pastInextensible_iff.2 hγ` gives C.dual.PastInextensible W (-I) (t ↦ γ (-t)), `CurveOn.neg (hchr (-b) hb (-a) ha)` makes the reversed curve chronal for C.dual, hA gives ⋃ t ∈ -I, C.dual.Iplus W {γ (-t)} = W, and the reindexing t ↦ -t (neg_neg, Set.mem_neg) with C.dual.Iplus = C.Iminus (dual_Iplus, rfl) finishes.

declarations.name: Causal.timelikeLine_posHalfLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq
declarations.statement: ∀ (I : Set ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ), timelikeLine.FutureInextensible posHalfLine I γ → (∀ a ∈ I, ∀ b ∈ I, timelikeLine.ChronalCurveOn posHalfLine γ a b) → ⋃ t ∈ I, timelikeLine.Iminus posHalfLine {γ t} = ↑posHalfLine
declarations.what: (A⁻) on W = (0, ∞) of the timelike line, a theorem of its own so that the keeper can cite it. Its type is exactly the hypothesis hA of GloballyHyperbolic.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeA at C = timelikeLine, W = posHalfLine (it is passed there with no adaptation in (c)).
declarations.proof: As the target says. (1) (A⁻) on ℝ (timelikeLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq_univ, FlrwType) is (A) for timelikeLine.dual at ⊤, by dual_iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_futureInextensible; `= ↑⊤` and `= univ` are bridged by Opens.coe_top both ways. (2) After `rw [← exp_rangeOpens_eq]`, exp_isSpacetimeExtension.dual.iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_pastInextensible carries it to (0, ∞) for timelikeLine.dual; `exact` closes, since hι.dual.rangeOpens = hι.rangeOpens is rfl. (3) The converse (a) reads it back for timelikeLine. The hypothesis hA fed to (a) is proved in step (2) by the transport from ℝ, not from (b), so nothing is circular.

non_vacuity.c_hypotheses_discharged: (c) has no hypothesis of its own: every hypothesis of GloballyHyperbolic.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeA is discharged on the concrete instance M = ℝ, C = timelikeLine, W = posHalfLine = (0, ∞): [T2Space ℝ] by instance, hT by timelikeLine_tarentin (Causal/Lines.lean:177), hG by timelikeLine_globallyHyperbolic (Causal/Lines.lean:172), and hA, (A⁻) on (0, ∞), by the new theorem (b). Probe.lean restates each as an `example` and re-derives (c) from them with W := posHalfLine named explicitly.
non_vacuity.a_used_with_a_hypothesis_that_holds: In the proof of (b), (a) is applied at C = timelikeLine, W = posHalfLine to hA: (A) for timelikeLine.dual on (0, ∞), which is proved there by transport from ℝ (exp_isSpacetimeExtension.dual.iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_pastInextensible applied to (A) for timelikeLine.dual at ⊤, itself from timelikeLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq_univ). Probe.lean also states that hypothesis as a theorem, probe_dual_posHalfLine_iUnion_Iplus_eq.
non_vacuity.the_A_minus_hypothesis_is_not_vacuous: (A⁻) on (0, ∞) could hold vacuously if (0, ∞) had no future-inextensible chronal curve. It has one: Probe.lean proves that Real.exp over ℝ is a chronal curve of posHalfLine on every segment (probe_exp_chronal, by timelikeLine_chronalCurveOn_iff: strictly increasing, continuous, positive) and is future-inextensible in posHalfLine (probe_exp_futureInextensible, by LineDevelopment.futureInextensible_of_not_tendsto_atTop, since exp tends to +∞ and so has no limit in (0, ∞)). (b) then gives the concrete instance ⋃ t, I⁻(exp t, (0, ∞)) = (0, ∞). Likewise (a)'s hypothesis is not vacuous: t ↦ exp (−t) over ℝ is a past-inextensible chronal curve of (0, ∞) for timelikeLine.dual (dual_pastInextensible_iff, neg_univ), and the probe checks ⋃ t, I⁺_dual(exp (−t), (0, ∞)) = (0, ∞) for it. These checks import Causal.LineDevelopment and Causal.TimelikeHomotopy (ETT layer) in the probe only; the module's imports are unchanged.
non_vacuity.what_the_witness_shows: As for the other witnesses on the timelike line, (c) shows the hypotheses of the theorem consistent (jointly satisfiable on a concrete model), not FutureBoundaryChart inhabited there: timelikeLine_not_futureBoundaryChart (FlrwType) proves that no open set of the timelike line has a future boundary chart. The predicate is inhabited elsewhere: Causal.minkowski_pastBoundaryChart, read at (minkowski n).dual through Causality.dual_dual (rfl), is a FutureBoundaryChart (T-abs-flrw-future-extension, corrected_after_audit), which is layer 3 and not imported.

findings: No paper label is involved. These findings concern the programme.

The converse (a) needs no hypothesis: (A⁻) for C on W and (A) for C.dual on W are equivalent for every causality and every open W, with no separation axiom. Probe.lean checks the iff from the two directions. The library has no iff form; none was added, since the target asks for the converse and every consumer needs one direction.

(b) carries the chronal-on-segments hypothesis, in the shape of hA, because the transport IsSpacetimeExtension.iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_pastInextensible reads the curve back in the source through it. (A⁻) on ℝ (timelikeLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq_univ) has no such hypothesis. Whether it can be dropped on (0, ∞) was not examined: hA asks for it, so (b) is exactly what the theorem applied needs.

(c), like the other witnesses on the timelike line, shows the theorem's hypotheses consistent, not the chart inhabited (timelikeLine_not_futureBoundaryChart). With it, every closed-ambient globally hyperbolic form in the module has a kb/0011 witness on W = (0, ∞): (A), (B), (B⁻) and now (A⁻).

Use it to show that an (A)-type hypothesis on (0, ∞) is not vacuous (campaign/T-abs-flrw-future-a-witness/Probe.lean).
